feeds.title: History Today
feeds.description: History Today is one of the worlds leading serious history magazine.The publication is based in London and published monthly.Every contribution is carefully edited and illustrated to make the magazine a pleasurable, as well as an informative, read.

feeds.title: On History Blog
feeds.description: On History is a digital magazine produced by the Institute of Historical Research, the national centre for the study of history in the UK. Our aim is to publish accessible and engaging articles that reflect on contemporary issues facing our discipline and deepen public understanding of the past.

feeds.title: The History Blog
feeds.description: Hello, I am Livius. I created this history blog page because my interests are primarily European ancient and medieval. Here I am providing general blogs on history, historical podcasts, historical illustrations, ancient books, and many more. I also intend to make a note of all the topically relevant books I read, and a list of all the topically relevant books sitting in a pile glaring at me.

feeds.title: The Royal Watcher Blog
feeds.description: Hello, I am Saad, 20, Founder & Editor of The Royal Watcher, Royal Contributor for ELLE and an Art History Student. The Royal Watcher is a place to learn and share everything we know and like about Royals!

feeds.title: The History Girls
feeds.description: The History Girls are a group of best-selling, award-winning writers of historical fiction and non-fiction. Some of us write for young adults, some for fully fledged adults, some for younger readers.

feeds.title: Past and Present
feeds.description: Past and Present details religious and cultural history of early modern Britain, and the impact of the Reformation. It is widely acknowledged to be the liveliest and most stimulating historical journal in the English-speaking world.

feeds.title: Stuff About London
feeds.description: StuffAboutLondon is a blog on London history. It is a collection of random posts and photographs about things that Don Brown has found interesting, puzzling, entertaining or just noteworthy about London.

feeds.title: Living London History Blog
feeds.description: Sharing London's curiosities, hidden gems and historical walks, oddities and self-guided walks to help curious wanderers explore the city. The focus is on the history that is hiding in plain sight and helping Londoners and visitors better connect with the history of this incredible city.

feeds.title: The British Newspaper Archive Blog
feeds.description: Explore in these updates an array of amazing finds and news from over 300 years of historical newspapers. Read entertaining, quirky tidbits about the life and times covered by these papers. The British Newspaper Archive is a partnership between the British Library and Findmypast to digitize the British Library's vast collection of newspapers.

feeds.title: HistoryExtra
feeds.description: HistoryExtra brings you the most exciting, extraordinary, and captivating stories from Britain's history and beyond. Find thousands of historical articles on both British and world history for all levels of knowledge and interest.HistoryExtra is the official website for BBC History Magazine, BBC History Revealed and BBC World Histories Magazine.

feeds.title: Essex Record Office Blog
feeds.description: The Essex Record Office is the storehouse of Essex history. We look after documents, maps, images and sound and video recordings that together tell the story of nearly 1,000 years of our county's past. We use our blog to publish highlights from our collection, share research tips, and offer peeks behind-the-scenes at our work looking after this unique collection.

feeds.title: Centre for Kent History and Heritage Blog
feeds.description: The Centre for Kent History and Heritage (CKHH) showcases the research of Historians, Literary Scholars, and Archaeologists in the School of Humanities. The Centre's weekly blog provides news, reports, and research, offering a treasure trove of material valued by its international following.

feeds.title: The History of England Blog
feeds.description: The History of England Blog by David Crowther recounts Historic moments, travels, and events that shaped centuries. David is a history graduate and loves to talk about history. Through his blog and podcast, he aims to cover all of Britain's history - from the cataclysmic end of Roman Britain to the present day.

feeds.title: A Bit About Britain Blog
feeds.description: A Bit About Britain's blog features articles about places to visit in Britain, British history, events in Britain - and more. It is a personal, independent, project that seeks to inspire, inform and entertain. It provides a portal into Britain's history, heritage, and landscape, tells stories that put places and events into context and appeals to armchair travellers, and visitor alike.

feeds.title: Love British History
feeds.description: Photos, facts, and debates on the best of British history along with historical recipes for you to try at home. Jo Romero is a lover of early modern history with a degree in Modern History. Here she shares her thought about History, Sketches, Food, Travel and more.

feeds.title: European Royal History
feeds.description: This blog will mainly focus on the past but I will deliver current news about both the reigning and non-reigning royal families in Europe. The author of this blog has had an interest in European royalty since the late 1970s. My main interest is in British Royalty but I am also interested in all the monarchies of Europe past and present.

feeds.title: BBC History Research Blog
feeds.description: Every year the BBC opens its archives to a wide range of academics researching the BBC's role in national and international history. Their research leads to bestselling books, academic papers and in-depth journalistic articles. This blog reveals the variety of BBC themes explored by academia.

feeds.title: University of Nottingham Blog » History Past and Present
feeds.description: This blog showcases research in the Department of History, setting out key points and arguments and highlighting the relevance of historical events in today's society.

feeds.title: Museum Facts
feeds.description: Whoever says history is boring wasn't taught history right. We believe in making history fun and easy to read by uncovering its quirky, bizarre facts and presenting to you with beautiful visuals.

feeds.title: Royal Splendor
feeds.description: This blog presents stories about royal history and the lives of interesting royals from the UK and Europe.

feeds.title: History Journal
feeds.description: History Journal is the official journal of the Historical Association. Our online offering is an extension of the Historical Association's work in public history and aims to make high-quality cutting-edge research accessible to the general public. Follow our blog updates to get more in-depth knowledge about the Journal and its work.

feeds.title: Yale University Press London Blog » British History
feeds.description: The official blog of Yale University Press, London. We publish history, politics, current affairs, art, architecture, biography, and pretty much everything else. Read interesting posts informing and commenting on Britain's History, Literature. Poetry, Culture, Kings and much more from the Medieval era.

feeds.title: The British Museum Blog
feeds.description: A museum of the world, for the world. Discover over two million years of human history and culture. The collections from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas and the ancient world include world-famous objects. An indepth information about British history, Follow for more!

feeds.title: History of government Blog
feeds.description: History of government is a blog that features articles from guest historians and civil servants about the history of UK government.

feeds.title: History Matters
feeds.description: History Matters is a shared blog from the Department of History, University of Sheffield. Written by Sheffield historians (staff, students, alumni, and friends), here you will find cutting-edge research, the history behind the headlines, and why we think history really matters.

feeds.title: HRP Blogs
feeds.description: Historic Royal Palaces is an independent charity that looks after the Tower of London, Hampton Court, the Banqueting House, Kensington Palace, Kew Palace and Hillsborough Castle.
